extraction.name: RoboFAC Dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale and diverse dataset for question-answering on robot failure videos, comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. The dataset includes six types of failures organized across three hierarchical levels (task planning, motion planning, execution control) and eight question types for task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Xiamen University, Harbin Institute of Technology Shenzhen)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Simulation data was collected using the ManiSkill environment for 14 robotic tasks, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. For each custom task, expert policies were defined by specifying target end-effector poses, with feasible trajectories generated using motion planning. Failure data was generated by replacing the original expert policy with code snippets producing erroneous trajectories at selected substages. Real-world data was collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm for 6 tasks. Each video was accompanied by a corresponding textual description including the substage where failure occurred, failure taxonomy, and explanation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Software Collection, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Simulation environments (ManiSkill), objects from YCB Object Dataset, scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR, and real-world teleoperation data collected via SO-100 robotic arm using the lerobot framework with three synchronized viewpoints (wrist-mounted, top-down, and front-left cameras).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Failure data was generated by replacing the original expert policy with code snippets producing erroneous trajectories at selected substages, causing the overall robotic task to fail. Perturbations were added to end-effector poses to generate various failure types.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual data cleaning was performed to filter out trajectories where motion planning failed and did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions. Approximately 75% of the collected data was retained after cleaning.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Raw data was annotated to construct video-based QA samples corresponding to eight question types. For each question type, five question templates were provided. For five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from textual descriptions with well-defined ground truths. For the remaining three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, low-level correction), GPT-4o was used to generate reference answers from both video and textual description inputs. All GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: GPT-4o was used for generating reference answers; manual review was conducted by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All outputs from GPT-4o were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The integration of the RoboFAC model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless. The success rate of real-world tasks remains subject to further enhancement, largely due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions. The model is applied exclusively to VLA models in this work; hierarchical policies may require more targeted correction strategies.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of multimodal large models for robotic failure analysis and correction, including Task Understanding, Failure Analysis, and Failure Correction based on robot manipulation videos. The dataset was split with 60K QA pairs for training and 18K QA pairs (10K simulated and 8K real-world) for evaluation. Used as an external critic for VLA control pipelines to provide correction instructions for failure recovery.
